steps.a: Two ways to build it: load all rows and build the CSV string in memory, or stream rows from a Postgres cursor through a CSV transform into the response. For a 5,000-student class with ~40 quizzes that's ~200k rows, which would hold a lot in memory per request, so I'll stream with pg-query-stream and csv-stringify.

steps.a: Added a streaming CSV endpoint (Postgres cursor in batches of 1,000 piped through csv-stringify, connection released on finish or error) behind the existing teacher-of-class guard, plus a Download CSV button in the gradebook toolbar. Tests cover the row count and the 403 for other teachers; a 200k-row benchmark finished in 3.8 s with about 31 MB extra memory.

reference.summary: Added a gradebook CSV download: an Express endpoint that streams rows from a Postgres cursor through a CSV stringifier to the response, guarded by the existing teacher authorisation, plus a toolbar button. Tests for output and authorisation pass and a 200k-row benchmark ran in under 4 seconds with modest memory.
facts: The endpoint streams rows with a Postgres query stream in batches of 1,000 through csv-stringify
It reuses the teacher-of-class guard and a test checks other teachers get 403
A Download CSV button was added to the gradebook toolbar
A benchmark of 200,000 rows took about 3.8 s with about 31 MB extra memory

decisions.choice: Stream rows from a cursor instead of building the CSV in memory
decisions.reason: large classes produce about 200k rows, too much to hold per request
